Implemented the cross-runtime court without touching the existing dirty performance campaign. Shared JVM/Scala.js registry: 23 representative public operations at side 64 and 21 fast-path operations at sides 256/1024; 8 families, 4 semantic dtypes, 6 layouts. Scala.js Long is correctness-only at side 64. Added dtype-specialized fixture/signature paths, Node argv forwarding, optional case progress, case-boundary explicit-GC control, pinned runtime metadata, samples/quartiles/RSD, and same-host comparator with every visible row and strict environment matching.

Verified current source: 65/65 JVM versus full-linked Node semantic rows match; Python comparator suite plus existing matrix tests 14/14; CrossRuntimeCourtSuite 6/6 JVM and 6/6 Scala.js; core 131/131 JVM and 131/131 Scala.js; laws 2/2 JVM and 2/2 Scala.js; browser 3/3; fullLinkJS passed; fmtCheck and git diff --check passed; browser guard clean before and after. A one-sample 1 ms Node timing smoke exercised 63 measured rows and 2 correctness-only Long rows but is explicitly not a baseline or performance claim.

Important harness findings fixed: Scala.js automatic main initialization passed empty args, unintentionally launching the default timed court; the Node platform now forwards process.argv. A Long logical checksum index made signature scans pathological on Scala.js; NDArray size is Int-bounded, so the exact accumulator now uses Int. Generic fixture/signature paths were also replaced with direct primitive setup and scans outside measured operations.

Remaining acceptance: on a calm host, run the documented full JVM NumPy matrix and GC profiler plus the full Node protocol (200 ms warmup, 250 ms samples, 7 samples, Node --expose-gc and separate --trace-gc diagnostics), check machine-readable receipts into a dated results directory, and characterize variance before establishing budgets. Do not close from the smoke receipt.
